subject: Backpressure + connection-handshake: field repro and mitigation plan
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
To: Pete Lowe <pete@brightlane.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Backpressure + connection-handshake: reproducer + ask

Hi Pete —

Thanks for the heads up on the intermittent 503s you and your SREs saw during peak traffic windows. We pulled the initial logs you uploaded and attached a small repro harness that should help us iterate quickly (handshake-repro-logs.tar.gz attached).

Quick summary of what we've seen from our side:
- Failures cluster around connection setup when concurrent streaming sessions spike (~>500 concurrent streams).
- The runtime sometimes stalls in the TLS handshake path; requests time out and the client sees immediate 503s rather than a graceful backoff.

As a next step I want to propose a short joint debugging run and an immediate mitigation path:
1) Can your SRE run the attached harness (replay at 75% and 110% of baseline) and share the pcap/logs?
2) Short-term mitigations we can deploy quickly:
   - Add a client-side jittered exponential backoff in the BrightLane client (recommend 50ms base, max 2s).
   - Increase server-side handshake timeout by 200ms for the affected pool.
   - Enable a conservative request-concurrency cap (soft limit) on the affected route so we return 429 instead of 503 when overloaded.

Longer-term we'd like to investigate adding a handshake admission controller in the runtime to protect the accept path. Karthik, any early thoughts on feasibility?

If you can share an SLA-friendly window this week, Hannah and Karthik and I can join for a 30–45m debug session.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: handshake-repro-logs.tar.gz (log bundle, 18MB)

From: Pete Lowe <pete@brightlane.com>

Cc: BrightLane SRE <sre@brightlane.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800

On Mon, Nov 9, 2026 at 09:12 AM Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Pete —
> 
> Thanks for the heads up on the intermittent 503s you and your SREs saw during peak traffic windows. We pulled the initial logs you uploaded...

Thanks Alex — appreciate the quick response and the repro package.

We've already captured a few pcap snippets from our canary cluster and see the same pattern: a burst of SYN/TLS ClientHello events followed by a subset that never complete the handshake. The spike correlates with a downstream batch job that causes a short CPU pressure window.

I attached our capture and two SRE traces (sre_trace.zip) showing timing and kernel-level drops. We can run your harness; prefer to do it Tuesday morning PT if that works.

Short-term we can implement the client-side jittered backoff; our SDK has a toggle for that. We're less comfortable returning 429s without a clear fallback on your side because some of these clients assume idempotency. If you can guarantee a 3xx/4xx/Retry-After behavior it will help.

Also: for auditing purposes, can one of you capture the exact runtime flags we should flip for "increase handshake timeout"? That will help our change control board.

--
Pete Lowe
Platform Engineering Manager, BrightLane
Attachment: sre_trace.zip (pcap + traces)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>, Pete Lowe <pete@brightlane.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 08:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Backpressure + connection-handshake: reproducer + ask

Thanks for the data, Pete — good signal. Quoting your point: "clients assume idempotency" — that's important and pushes us toward a more conservative server-side approach for the short-term.

Proposed short-term action items (24–72h):
- Alex: coordinate change control note for BrightLane to flip client-side jittered backoff (owner: BrightLane). Target: Tue morning test.
- Karthik/Runtime: provide exact runtime flags + a canary config that increases the handshake timeout by +200ms on the affected pool (owner: Karthik).
- Product/Support (me): prepare an MCC note and an SRE runbook entry that documents the 429 vs 503 behaviour and guidance for customers (owner: Hannah).

Medium-term (2–4 weeks):
- Build an admission-rate limiter for the handshake path in the runtime that gracefully rejects with Retry-After + clear metric emission. This would give you a clean signal to auto-throttle upstream clients without breaking semantics for idempotent callers.

I've attached a quick flowchart that sketches the mitigation path and the mutual-action-plan PDF with owners/dates.

When can BrightLane's SREs run Alex's harness? I'll block time on Wed if Tuesday doesn't work.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Product Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Pete Lowe <pete@brightlane.com>, Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Backpressure + connection-handshake: reproducer + ask

Pete / Alex / Hannah —

Thanks for the reproducer and traces. Quick technical readout and a candidate mitigation we can ship as a fast follow:

Findings (from repro + traces):
- The runtime accept loop isn't accounting for transient CPU stalls in our TLS worker pool; when workers back up, the handshake code path holds the socket in a WAIT state longer than the socket-level timeout, which manifests as an apparent immediate 503 to the caller.
- There's no coherent admission control during the accept/handshake phase today (we rely on kernel queues + worker threads).

Candidate short-term patch (canary in 24–48h):
- Add a lightweight semaphore limiter on handshake-entry with a small queue (size 32) + fast-fail to 429 when full. Emit metric: runtime.handshake.admissions and runtime.handshake.rejections.
- Expose two runtime flags: --handshake-admit-limit and --handshake-queue-ms. For your change control board, toggles would be: --handshake-admit-limit=256 --handshake-queue-ms=200 (defaults remain unchanged).

Example behavior snippet:
```
if (!handshake_semaphore.try_acquire()) {
  // soft-fail and send Retry-After header
  return respond(429).withHeader("Retry-After", "0.5");
}
```

Rollout plan:
- Build + internal canary (staging) 24h, run BrightLane harness against staging.
- If staging looks good, canary 10% of production traffic on your affected pool for 6h.
- Collect metrics and iterate on admit-limit.

I can produce a patch PR today and a canary manifest. Pete — if you approve the test plan I'll start the PR and coordinate a staging window.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Engineer, Runtime | Redwood Inference
